claim: Lassas-Lu-Yamaguchi (2024) prove the only known quantitative-stability theorem for a spectral inverse problem on a Riemannian orbifold, with an explicit Gromov-Hausdorff modulus of continuity of triple-logarithmic type.
stance_target: quantitative stability results exist for spectral inverse problems on orbifolds
scope_conditions: Riemannian orbifolds arising as 1-dimensional Gromov-Hausdorff collapses of n-manifolds with bounded diameter, sectional curvature, and third covariant derivative of curvature (class MM(n,Lambda,Lambda3,D))
quoted_support: the finite interior spectral data {λj, ϕj|U}δ−1 j=0 for δ < bδ determine a finite metric space b X such that dGH(X \ Sσ,δ, b X) < C1(X, σ) / (log log | log δ|)^{-C2}

claim: The Lassas-Lu-Yamaguchi stability bound is triple-logarithmic (inverse of an iterated logarithm to a power), a far weaker modulus of continuity than the single-logarithmic stability standard in Calderon-type inverse boundary value problems.
stance_target: the strength/modulus of stability achievable in geometric spectral inverse problems
scope_conditions: reconstruction of a collapsed orbifold limit from finite interior spectral data
quoted_support: dGH(X \ Sσ,δ, b X) < C1(X, σ) / (log log | log δ|)^{-C2}, ... The constant C1(X, σ) depends on σ, r0, n, Λ, Λ3, D, v0 as well as the space X, and C1(X, σ) →∞ as σ →0.

claim: The quantitative stability in Theorem 1.2 rests on a quantitative unique-continuation estimate for the wave operator (Theorem 1.3) with an exponential-type bound exp(h^{-C5}), an improvement over prior results by removing assumptions on covariant derivatives of the curvature tensor.
stance_target: technique used to prove quantitative stability of spectral reconstruction on orbifolds
scope_conditions: closed smooth n-manifold (Y,g) with C^2 metric, bounded curvature, diameter, volume from below; weighted Laplacian and non-homogeneous wave equation

claim: Part I of this paper (Kurylev-Lassas-Lu-Yamaguchi, arXiv:1209.5875) proves uniqueness of the inverse problem and only a qualitative continuity/stability statement for the collapsing-manifold-to-orbifold limit, with no explicit modulus of continuity; the explicit quantitative bound is new to Part II (2024).
stance_target: the finding that quantitative (not merely qualitative) stability for orbifold spectral inverse problems is a recent (2024) and rare result
scope_conditions: n-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with bounded diameter and sectional curvature, collapsing to a lower-dimensional stratified limit space in measured Gromov-Hausdorff topology
quoted_support: In the part I of the paper, we proved the uniqueness of the inverse problem and a continuity result for the stability in the closure of Riemannian manifolds with bounded diameter and sectional curvature in the measured Gromov-Hausdorff topology. In this paper we show that when the collapse of dimension is 1-dimensional, it is possible to obtain quantitative stability of the inverse problem for Riemannian orbifolds.

claim: The orbifold reconstruction setting in Lassas-Lu-Yamaguchi is abstract (interior spectral data of the weighted Laplacian on an open subset of a general n-1 dimensional orbifold limit space), structurally disjoint from recovering a finite set of discrete cone-order/cone-angle invariants from finitely many symmetric functions of the Laplace spectrum (heat invariants).
stance_target: whether existing orbifold stability results directly cover finite-discrete-invariant recovery (e.g. cone orders from S1, R, P3)
scope_conditions: Riemannian orbifolds as measured Gromov-Hausdorff limits, dim(X)=n-1
quoted_support: Note that the incomplete data case of the theorem above is of an asymptotic nature as the reconstruction is done to a fixed orbifold.
